hero.headline: Get your own
hero.intro: This whole site is open source. Download it, change it, and fill it with your own prompts. It works for one person or a team.

items.title: Complete source code
items.description: All of the code, including the interface and the way prompts are stored. Built with Astro, React and Tailwind CSS.

items.title: Content in files
items.description: Prompts, personas and posts are plain Markdown files in the repository. Add a file to add an entry.

items.title: Light and dark mode
items.description: Both themes are included, and the layout works on phones and desktops.

items.title: Any static host
items.description: The site builds to static files, so it runs on GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel or your own server.

items.title: Change anything
items.description: The name, wordmark and navigation are set in src/data/branding.json. Page copy is in src/data, and plate wording is set where each plate is used.

about.label: Open source
about.headline: What open source means
paragraphs: Open source software is code that anyone can read, use and change. Think of a recipe that is shared freely: you can follow it exactly or swap ingredients.

The project uses the MIT license, which lets you use it for personal or commercial work as long as you keep the license notice. The theme code in src/components/kojima adds a Commons Clause: you can use it in your own site, but not resell the template as is.

items.question: Do I need to be a developer?
items.answer: Some comfort with the command line helps. The README covers installing and building the site. Larger changes are easier with a developer.

items.question: How much does it cost to run?
items.answer: It can be free. The site is static, so it runs on free static hosting such as GitHub Pages. The forms use Web3Forms, which has a free tier.

items.question: Can I remove the branding?
items.answer: Yes. The name and links are in src/data/branding.json. Keep the license notices when you change the rest.

items.question: Is open source the same as free?
items.answer: Not quite. Open source means you can see and change the code. Free means no cost. This project is both.

items.question: Can I use it for a business?
items.answer: Yes. Commercial use is allowed if you keep the license notices. You can't resell the template itself as is, because the theme code has a Commons Clause.

items.question: Is there support?
items.answer: No ongoing support. This is a personal project. You can report bugs or ask for features on GitHub, and I will look when I can.

items.question: Can I contribute changes?
items.answer: Yes. If you fix a bug or add a feature, you are welcome to send it back on GitHub.

header.label: Contact
header.title: Need help getting started?
header.description: Read the README on GitHub first. For anything else, send me a message.
